# Final verification using Pearson correlation formula with sample correlation (n-1 denominator)
import math

balance_12 = [3414, 3812, 3705, 2171, 3765, 3572, 3739, 4581, 4277, 5924, 4873, 3869]
unemployment = [6.6, 6.9, 6.9, 7.0, 7.1, 6.9, 7.0, 6.6, 6.7, 6.5, 6.1, 6.0]

n = len(balance_12)

mean_balance = sum(balance_12) / n
mean_unemployment = sum(unemployment) / n

# Covariance with n-1
covariance = sum((b - mean_balance) * (u - mean_unemployment) for b, u in zip(balance_12, unemployment)) / (n - 1)

# Std with n-1
std_balance = math.sqrt(sum((b - mean_balance) ** 2 for b in balance_12) / (n - 1))
std_unemployment = math.sqrt(sum((u - mean_unemployment) ** 2 for u in unemployment) / (n - 1))

pearson_corr = covariance / (std_balance * std_unemployment)

print(f"Sample correlation (n-1): {pearson_corr}")
print(f"Rounded: {round(pearson_corr, 2)}")

# Population correlation (n)
covariance_pop = sum((b - mean_balance) * (u - mean_unemployment) for b, u in zip(balance_12, unemployment)) / n
std_balance_pop = math.sqrt(sum((b - mean_balance) ** 2 for b in balance_12) / n)
std_unemployment_pop = math.sqrt(sum((u - mean_unemployment) ** 2 for u in unemployment) / n)

pearson_corr_pop = covariance_pop / (std_balance_pop * std_unemployment_pop)

print(f"Population correlation (n): {pearson_corr_pop}")
print(f"Rounded: {round(pearson_corr_pop, 2)}")

# Most common is sample correlation (n-1) which gives -0.49
